reading.title: Linguistic Relativity and Language Structure
reading.passage: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, proposed in the early twentieth century, suggests that language fundamentally shapes how speakers perceive and conceptualize the world. This theory posits that linguistic structures constrain cognitive processes, meaning that speakers of different languages may literally think differently based on their language's grammar and vocabulary. For instance, languages with multiple words for snow, such as certain Inuit dialects, may enable speakers to perceive subtle distinctions in snow types that speakers of English, with its single term, do not readily recognize. Conversely, modern linguists argue that while language may influence cognition to some degree, the relationship is not deterministic. Research demonstrates that speakers can transcend linguistic limitations through conceptual metaphor and abstraction. Furthermore, cognitive development, cultural context, and individual experience play equally significant roles in shaping perception. The contemporary view recognizes language as one among many factors contributing to thought, rather than its sole determinant, suggesting a more nuanced understanding of the language-cognition relationship.

questions.q: According to the passage, what does the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis claim about language?
options: Language has no effect on perception
Language shapes how speakers perceive and conceptualize the world
Only certain languages influence thought
All speakers think identically regardless of language
questions.explanation: 지문의 첫 번째 문장에서 '언어가 근본적으로 화자들의 세계 인식 및 개념화 방식을 형성한다'고 명시하고 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about speakers of languages with multiple words for snow?
options: They are more intelligent than other speakers
They may perceive subtle distinctions in snow types more readily than English speakers
They cannot learn English
They invented snow themselves
questions.explanation: 지문에서 여러 개의 눈 단어를 가진 언어의 화자들이 영어 사용자들이 인식하지 못하는 눈의 미묘한 차이를 지각할 수 있다고 설명합니다.

questions.q: The word 'transcend' in the second paragraph is closest in meaning to
options: Accept
Overcome or go beyond
Strengthen
Ignore
questions.explanation: 'transcend'은 '넘어서다, 초월하다'라는 뜻으로, 여기서는 언어의 제한을 극복할 수 있다는 의미입니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention 'cognitive development, cultural context, and individual experience' in the final sentences?
options: To prove the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis is completely correct
To suggest that language is the only factor affecting thought
To indicate that multiple factors besides language influence perception
To explain why Inuit languages are superior
questions.explanation: 저자는 이러한 요소들을 언급함으로써 언어가 사고에 영향을 미치는 유일한 요소가 아니며, 다양한 요소들이 역할을 한다는 현대적 관점을 제시합니다.

sentences.original: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, proposed in the early twentieth century, suggests that language fundamentally shapes how speakers perceive and conceptualize the world.
sentences.paraphrase: Proposed during the early 1900s, the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis proposes that the way speakers understand and interpret the world is fundamentally determined by their language.
sentences.tip: 관사 변경 및 술어 동사 치환('shapes'→'is determined by'), 단어 순서 재배열을 통한 패러프레이즈

sentences.original: For instance, languages with multiple words for snow, such as certain Inuit dialects, may enable speakers to perceive subtle distinctions in snow types that speakers of English, with its single term, do not readily recognize.
sentences.paraphrase: As an example, speakers of languages like some Inuit dialects, which contain numerous terms for snow, might be able to detect fine differences among types of snow that English speakers, who use only one word, cannot easily identify.
sentences.tip: 문장 구조 단순화(복잡한 전치사구→명확한 절), 동의어 사용('multiple'→'numerous', 'perceive'→'detect', 'subtle'→'fine')

sentences.original: Research demonstrates that speakers can transcend linguistic limitations through conceptual metaphor and abstraction.
sentences.paraphrase: Studies show that individuals are capable of overcoming the constraints imposed by their language by using abstract thinking and figurative language.
sentences.tip: 능동 주어 유지하되 술어 변경('demonstrates'→'show'), 동의어 사용('transcend'→'overcome', 'limitations'→'constraints'), 구체적 설명 추가

sentences.original: The contemporary view recognizes language as one among many factors contributing to thought, rather than its sole determinant.
sentences.paraphrase: Modern scholars understand language to be merely one of numerous influences on thinking, not the only force that shapes it.
sentences.tip: 현대적 표현('contemporary'→'Modern'), 구조 단순화(비교 구조 명확화), 동의어 사용('factors'→'influences', 'determinant'→'force')

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer shopping online. Others prefer shopping in physical stores. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details in your response.
model_sentences: I definitely prefer shopping in physical stores because it offers a more personal and interactive experience.
First, when I shop in person, I can actually see and touch the products before buying them, which helps me make better purchasing decisions.
For example, when I bought clothes at a mall last month, I could try them on immediately to check the fit and color, whereas ordering online would have required multiple returns.
Additionally, I enjoy the immediate gratification of taking my purchases home right away instead of waiting for delivery.
Overall, despite online shopping's convenience, the ability to inspect products firsthand and enjoy instant possession makes physical stores my preferred shopping method.

listening.title: Dormitory Room Assignment Inquiry
listening.script:
Student A: Hi, I need to ask about my dormitory assignment. I applied for housing three weeks ago, but I haven't received any confirmation yet.

Administrator: Of course, I can help you with that. Let me check the system. Can you provide your student ID number?

Student A: It's 2847563.

Administrator: Thank you. I see your application here. It shows that you requested a double room on campus, correct?

Student A: Yes, I did. I preferred a double room because I thought it would be more social. But I'm becoming concerned about the timeline. When will assignments be finalized?

Administrator: Assignments are typically completed by late August. However, due to high demand this year, we're processing requests sequentially. You should expect notification by email within the next two weeks.

Student A: Okay, that's helpful. One more thing—if I don't get a double room, can I request a single room instead?

Administrator: Absolutely. You can submit a modification request through the housing portal, and we'll reassign you accordingly. Any other concerns?

Student A: No, that was very informative. Thank you for your help!

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: To discuss the quality of dormitory facilities
To inquire about the status of a dormitory room assignment
To complain about housing fees
To request a transfer to a different campus
questions.explanation: 학생이 기숙사 배정 상태를 확인하기 위해 행정 담당자에게 문의하는 대화입니다.

questions.q: When does the administrator say dormitory assignments will typically be completed?
options: Within one week
By mid-August
By late August
In September
questions.explanation: 행정 담당자가 '기숙사 배정은 일반적으로 8월 말경에 완료된다'고 명시합니다.

questions.q: Why does the student prefer a double room?
options: Because it is less expensive
Because it provides more privacy
Because it would be more social
Because it is closer to campus facilities
questions.explanation: 학생이 '더 사회적일 것 같다고 생각해서 더블 룸을 원했다'고 언급합니다.
